metadata.title: Notice to industry: Clarification of section 4.3 of the "Reporting adverse reactions to Marketed Health Products" Guidance Document for Industry
metadata.legal_basis: Agency guidance or notice under the Food and Drug Regulations; legislation prevails.
metadata.applicability: Applicants, sponsors and market authorization holders reporting ICSRs (see the PV Info ICSR rulebook for scope).

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.
Candidates are not approved requirements. Read the original, qualifications and exceptions.
Scans, tables, other languages and implicit obligations may be missed. Zero candidates does not establish zero requirements.

candidates.anchor: Reports from foreign regulatory authority databases / paragraph-22
candidates.statement: You must report to Health Canada individual serious unexpected adverse reaction reports, which occurred outside of Canada; for example, those originating from foreign regulatory authorities.
candidates.context: Reports from foreign regulatory authority databases You are not required to submit ICSRs from these foreign databases if you can determine that the product is not yours, based on the following “Exclusion Criteria for Product Identification”:

candidates.anchor: Reports from foreign regulatory authority databases / paragraph-31
candidates.statement: If unable to determine if the product is yours, then you should presume that it is, report the ICSR to us, and indicate that you couldn't identify the specific brand.
candidates.context: Note: You may also apply these “Exclusion Criteria for Product Identification” to foreign adverse reaction reports coming from any sources; for example, scientific literature reports.
